new_statements.relation_note: Three-tone system 55/33/21 evidenced in 699 forms and an explicit tone-reflex table; tense vs lax phonation noted; no stress statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Aluo (Alo of Wuding Dongpo Yichidan, data from Chen Kang 2010) is analysed as a lexical tone language with three level/falling tones — high 55, mid 33, low(-falling) 21 (plus a marginal 11 in two items) — assigned by Proto-Ngwi category: *1 > 21 (33 after certain prefixed/preglottalised initials), *2 > 33 (55 after preglottalised/s-prefixed initials), *3 > 21, checked *H > 21, checked *L > 55, with tense phonation in the *L (checked) reflexes. Nothing is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Split reflexes by initial class (e.g. *1 nasals/voiceless stops 21/33; *2 nasals/voiceless stops 33/55); cells 'nc'/'nd' = no cognate/no data.
new_statements.identity_note: Datapoint 'Alo', Subbranch Northern, Cluster Nasoid, source 'Chen 2010' wordlist, Yunnan > Chuxiong > Wuding > Dongpo > Yichidan, 'datapoint listed in YYFC 1983'. Dongpo Township, NW Wuding, is Aluo territory (Gao 2017 recorded Aluo at Dongpo Lujiga); Glottolog maps Chen 2010's 'Alo' to Aluo [yna]. Not the Taloid Naluo/Naruo (nalu1239). | 'about 30,000 Laka (sometimes known to the Chinese as Gan Yi)' among small Northern Loloish languages near Nasu = Aluo [yna] (Laka/Gan Yi are Aluo's exonyms per ISO CR 2007-101 and Bradley 2007); group-level statement [name in source: Laka (Gan Yi); pages 39 (tree), 43 (text), 59 (appendix); group statements 38, 42]
